summary: NoMissingSession, KeepsSession, NeverAnother and MoveLeavesChoice hold for the current SidecarManager within 1-2 stored sessions, 3-5 new ids and 4-6 spawns (13,255 and 417,625 states), with the start gate and in-omp switch_session/new_session modeled. Code before a10eb6877 breaks KeepsSession; a10eb6877 breaks NeverAnother (F1); the code before the F2 fix breaks NeverAnother after an in-omp new_session and KeepsSession after a switch_session. F1 and F2 were reproduced as failing tests and fixed.

modeled: restart with no session, a stored session, another folder
stock writing a session and its autoResume (environment)
the start gate's restart into a worktree
switch_session and new_session inside the running omp
abstracted: the pool's view of the session is the ghost `shown`
an omp update's restart is Restart
out_of_scope: extensions and settings of a spawn
assumptions: A1: start()'s awaits do not change #sessionPath or #isNew
A2: get_state names the session the running omp is on
A3: autoResume picks only a written session of the folder
A4: the pool's sessionFile equals #sessionPath after the same get_state
A5: a fork, branch or handoff keeps #sessionPath on its parent until get_state names the copy; a crash in between reopens the parent, which is written and intact

findings.title: A new tab whose omp crashed before naming its session could come back on another conversation
findings.story: A new tab starts: its omp boots on a new session (n1). The ready frame clears #isNew (a10eb6877 did it in #handleReady). The omp crashes before the ready status's get_state answer reaches #observeResponse, so #sessionPath is still empty. The crash restart's sessionOpen then sees no session and a tab that is not new, and passes neither --session nor --config fresh-launch.yml: with the person's autoResume on, stock reopens the folder's most recent session (s1) in the tab that showed a new one. Fix: #isNew is cleared where get_state names the session, not at ready.

reproduction.test: src/main/session-launch-parity.test.ts::a new tab whose omp crashed before it named its session starts a new one, never another session

findings.title: An omp that crashed right after an in-tab switch_session or new_session came back on the session before it
findings.story: A tab is on session s1. The person starts a new session in it (new_session) or opens another one in the same tab (switch_session). Stock's answer names no file, so #sessionPath stays s1 until the next get_state; the pool already shows the switched-to session. The omp crashes before that get_state: the crash restart reopens s1, and the tab silently goes back to the conversation the person left (after new_session: the old one instead of the new empty one). Fix: #observeResponse takes switch_session's requested path, and after new_session clears the path and marks the tab new, so the restart starts a new session.

reproduction.test: src/main/session-launch-parity.test.ts::an omp that crashed after a switch_session comes back on the session switched to; ...after a new_session comes back on a new session, never the one before it
